one_liner: A fantasy-football-like software system for financial advisors trading securities (stocks, bonds, etc.)
abstract:
We have set out to create a game with GreenHill, the small Investment Reporting firm based in Maryland. They want us to create a fantasy league for financial advisors so they can trade stocks without the risk of losing it all. This game is meant to be hosted on a website and/or a mobile application. It will allow GreenHill to host advising competitions among Financial advisors that the employees personally invite to compete in. They will be able to buy stocks of a specific financial indices (i.e. Nasdaq, S&P500, etc.) with a set amount of virtual cash (specified by GreenHill). Their performance will be determined by the profit they accrue compared to the index and the best performing advisor wins glory and/or a prize established by GreenHill in the beginning of the competition!

We will be using technologies such as NodeJs, ReactJs, AWS EC2, AWS RDS for MySQL, and Figma to complete this project for the stakeholder.

one_liner: Mortgage CLO Extraction Web App for Bloomberg
abstract: Bloomberg L.P. is a financial, software, data, and media company. The Company provides financial software tools such as an analytics and equity trading platform, data services, and news to financial companies and organizations. Bloomberg receives mortgage collateralized loan obligations (CLO) as unstructured PDFs from several different sources. Currently, Bloomberg wants to know the transactions (buys and sells) of the mortgage CLOs. The manual process of extracting this information from unstructured PDFs is very time-consuming and labor-intensive. Thus, a method is needed to automate the extraction of the transaction data from the PDFs into a more compact and easier-to-read format like a CSV. \n\nMortgage CLO Extraction Web App is a web application built on top of a machine learning model that is in charge of extracting the transaction data from the unstructured PDFs into CSVs. This web application provides a graphic user interface that enables users to create and log in with individual accounts to upload mortgage CLO PDFs to be processed by the machine learning model. When the extraction process is completed, it uploads the CSVs to GIGwork for validation and notifies the user that they can download the resulting CSVs. In addition, users can also view their PDFs and CSVs on the web application and remove uploaded mortgage CLO PDFs from their accounts.

one_liner: A dynamic web application to handle the Senior Project sequence at Drexel.
abstract: Every year the senior class of students in Drexel’s CCI department have to go through senior project which lasts the 3-quarter duration of their senior year at Drexel. This process starts before senior year when the professors in charge of senior project hosts informational sessions for the incoming senior class roughly 6-7 months before senior year begins. In the time before the start of the project, students form into groups based off of their interests in specific project types. These include projects for Drexel, research, corporate partners with total project numbers reaching up to 60 as the number of projects is not static due to class size and variable team size per project.\n\nOnce the senior project begins students form a team using the CCI senior project site, select (or propose) a project and create a sub-page on the website detailing their project and team. The best projects are judged in a competition by a panel of industry judges to determine the best projects of that year. Currently all of these processes are handled by the professors in charge of senior project and done through other platforms like discord or by hand on the current CCI senior project site. This new site supports the automation of many senior project processes.

Users will be able to fill 2 pairs of a maximum of 10 traits to describe themselves and their ideal teammate. Based on that, Player 2's new matchmaking mode will return a list of users that match that user's preferences. one_liner: CollabArt is a collaborative gigapixel artwork exploration application.
abstract: Large pieces of artwork can be hard to immediately grasp and explore in depth due to their vast size. It is difficult to investigate this artwork, especially in a learning environment when you are not physically in front of it. The CollabArt Web App seeks to remove much of the prior friction by introducing a proprietary Gigapixel canvas. CollabArt allows users to develop a deeper understanding of large artworks by being able to explore, annotate, and comment on them. This is achieved by being able to view the artwork in extreme detail and having the ability to add annotations with supplementary content, including the option for groups to discuss the annotations. Culminating in the opportunity for users to create interactive stories derived from existing annotations and share this for external consumption. The power of investigation and storytelling is put in the hands of the user.

one_liner: A monster is roaming the halls... in this 3D first person horror game you need to escape the lodge in which this creature roams.
abstract:
Shady Creak Lodge is a first-person horror game made in Unreal Engine 5. 

You are Quinlan Keep, a contractor who has found himself in over his head, trapped in the remote Shady Creak Lodge, in which a dark, enigmatic creature stalks. This creature seems to be blind to all darkness, including the shadows cast by the very furniture in the lodge. In order to survive, you must move furniture to change the shadows cast in your environment, allowing yourself to hide in the most advantageous positions possible while shadow-hopping your way through the lodge. As you explore the lodge and attempt to escape, you will find that not all is as it seems, as nothing can escape the lodge unchanged.

one_liner: In-app reporting mechanism and a company-side helpdesk platform for Player 2 agents to be able to connect with users, access and resopond to user generated reports.
abstract:
Player 2 is a social networking platform where users can connect and interact in the form of text, images, and videos. Platforms with inadequate or ineffective content moderation measures face stiff consequences, such as brand boycotts and reduced trust among users. As scrutiny mounts, smaller platforms might have greater success luring advertisers by positioning themselves as trusted environments. Player 2 HelpDesk provides a robust content reporting and moderating mechanism to ensure the safety of users and advertising brands.

Our solution includes an in-app reporting mechanism and a company-side dashboard to manage user reports. This enables users to report a piece of content by opening a drop-down menu and selecting a category that best describes the violation. Once a user submits their report, it will generate a ticket on the company-side dashboard and assign it to an agent. Agents will be able to view all the tickets assigned to them and click on a ticket to expand it and view all the information before taking appropriate action. The help-desk platform will allow agents to connect, assist, and resolve any user's issues. After reviewing a ticket, agents can enforce content removal, strikes, and bans in accordance with the terms of service policy. Depending on the infraction, a user may receive anywhere from one to three strikes and if a user has a total of 3 or more strikes on their account, it will result in a ban from the Player 2 platform. The system includes an appeal that allows for the reversal of strikes, pending approval of an apology. Additionally, the Player 2 help desk provides statistical analysis of the report data. These analytics will better help admins understand user behaviors and trends in the Player 2 platform.

one_liner: SmartBard provides those visually impaired from Overbrook School for the Blind to access content that would be normally difficult to visually see on a traditional bulletin board through various accessibility features.
abstract: This application offers an accessible way to view different items that are traditionally placed on a bulletin board (i.e., announcements, pictures, etc.). Content on the bulletin board is accessible through various accessibility features (i.e., font size, contrast, audio, etc.), which are customized per user. In addition, users may request to add content to the bulletin board. The application consists of two groups of users, Students, and Administrators. Students request content to be added and Administrators moderate all content on the bulletin board by approving, rejecting, editing, and removing any requests.

one_liner: Mobile Application for Nursing Students
abstract: The Nursing Companion App is a mobile application for both iOS and Android that enables these nursing students to search and locate the material that is relevant to their studies. This material is delivered in the format of short videos (5-10 minutes) that are uploaded and curated by the professors of the nursing program. This mobile application has an associated web application that allows these professors to upload, tag, and add descriptions to the videos, as well as be able to remove them. The videos are sorted using various tags that are linked to them, such as part of the body, type of illness, or the class in which the material is being taught. Students also have the ability to search for videos directly using a provided search bar.

one_liner: Ponder utilizes node edge graphs to easily manage and visualize large sets of information required to run tabletop role-playing games.
abstract:
Ponder aims to solve the problem of having too much information to sift through during tabletop role-playing games. To achieve this, it displays sets of information inside nodes in a work area. Nodes can be anything from characters to items to events and more. Nodes are then connected to each other through edges that represent relationships. Graphs made up of nodes and edges are known as information networks and everything inside an information network can be expanded to display more information. 

Ponder is meant to be lightweight to be easily expanded on. This is on top of its already useful features such as: filtering to limit what node types you see, importing/exporting to easily share information networks among other users, and support for custom images to further how much information is readily available in one screen.

project_name: Electron Heating on Injection Fronts in the Earth’s Magnetotail: Analysis of THEMIS Data
one_liner: An analysis of electrons in the Earth’s magnetic tail using data collected from UCLA’s THEMIS satellites
abstract: Electron heating occurs among higher-energy electrons within the dipolarization, or injection fronts. These fronts occur in the magnetotail of the Earth, and they can be identified by location, a strong variance in the Bz component of the magnetic field, an increase in the electron flux, and an increase in electron temperature. The data was taken from UCLA’s THEMIS satellites A, D, and E, which are referred to as THA, THD, and THE, to look into possible events and draw insights. From this data, possible relationships have been identified between electron temperature (T_0), electron density (n_0*), and Bz. The goal for this research is to determine the cause for the increase of the temperature of electrons in injection fronts within the magnetotail of the Earth.

one_liner: Vulnerability assessment and remediation recommendations of the Drexel University network.
abstract: The vulnerability assessment of the Drexel University network involved scanning 131,068 IPs using Nmap, and filtering down to 648 hosts for vulnerability scans using OpenVAS and Vicarius. The assessment focused on the external facing network, such as public Wi-Fi networks and public webservers within the specified subnets. Detailed remediation recommendations were provided for each identified vulnerability, aimed at addressing root causes and significantly reducing associated risks. A follow-up assessment is recommended, with a focus on reviewing current documentation and patch management schedule and procedure. The report suggests that routine review of software usage could prevent many identified risks. The results and risk ratings were compiled into a report using identified techniques and software.

abstract: MeGo is a website designed to aid anyone traveling by providing information to help them properly prepare for a trip. Users can create trip plans on the website and view relevant information for those trips once created. MeGo provides information such as required paperwork, entry and exit restrictions, disease rates, and local norms (such as if masks are worn, required or suggested clothing, etc.). The website is tablet and mobile-friendly and will be accessible through most modern browsers.

one_liner: The nutritional assessment game is a web-based software created for nutritional science students to reinforce basic competencies while competing against their peers, along with analytical capture tools for instructors.
abstract: The nutritional assessment game will be a fully interactive web based app that will allow for students studying nutritional science to reinforce core competencies of the field while competing against their peers. The digital version of the nutritional assessment game will be built off of a physical version of the game created by Marylou McHugh. By incorporating critical competencies within the field of nutritional science with modern web based systems we seek to create an interactive learning experience that will encourage studying both inside and outside the classroom. In addition to being a studying tool the nutritional assessment game also seeks to help educators by providing analytical feedback about student competencies. This will allow instructors to track their students progress through the game allowing for greater insight into the knowledge base of each class.

one_liner: The Player 2 Web App is a web-based application that has been developed using NextJS and React Native Web.
abstract:
The Player 2 Web App is a cutting-edge web-based application developed to provide users with the same functionalities available on the Player 2 Mobile App. The app has been developed using NextJS and React Native Web technologies, making it user-friendly and accessible from any web browser.

One of the outstanding features of the Player 2 Web App is its ability to share components developed using Monorepo. This means that users can access different features on the app using shared components. This reduces the development time and makes the app more responsive.

In addition, the app has a landing page that provides users with information about the app. This includes details about the app's features, how to use it, and how to install it. Users can also access support and FAQs on the landing page.

Overall, the Player 2 Web App is a great tool for gamers and game enthusiasts who want to stay up-to-date with the latest news, reviews, and updates about their favorite games. Its user-friendly interface, accessibility, and shared components make it a great option for anyone who wants to stay connected to the gaming world.

one_liner: Motivated by advancements in spaceflight computing and the increasing efficacy of domain-adaptation techniques, this project will prove the adequacy of artificial intelligence for use in the automated identification of hazardous areas during spacecraft landing scenarios.
abstract:
This project will develop Keras artificial intelligence models trained on labeled data from computer-simulated surfaces of the asteroid Bennu, Mars, and the Moon. The goal of these models is to detect hazards on the surfaces of these objects, such as craters, mountains, rocks, and sand dunes. The development of simulated environments is required due to the restrictive dataset of available ground surface photography of these astronomical objects. The resulting trained models are validated against hand-labeled images of the real-world equivalents of our simulated environments. The simulations and Keras
models’ hyperparameters will be adjusted accordingly to guarantee best results. This project will then integrate these trained models with NASA’s flight software development platform. Further experimentation of both the trained models and their integration with flight software can determine their applicability in real spaceflight computing.

one_liner: Motion Tracker detects racewalkers in racewalking footage.
abstract:
Motion Tracker is a Python app that detects racewalkers in racewalking footage. Racewalking footage is used to train racewalking judges. Over the course of a race, racewalkers are video recorded at various points in the course. Since the video is constantly being recorded, there are lots of dead spaces in the footage where no racewalkers are walking across the course. Motion Tracker detects when racewalkers are present in the video, and cuts out all the dead space in the video.

one_liner: MineBound is a cross-disciplinary Minecraft mod with a primary focus on unique, fast-paced, real-time magic using a secondary configurable spell inventory and key binds.
abstract:
Spells can be combined through equipping either in the primary, secondary, or tertiary (configurable) slot, where each slot dictates use, either for active attacking/battle or passive defensive/utility capabilities. The gameplay loop of the mod will primarily consist of researching and crafting new spells, and strategically equipping them to get to the next tier of casting. 

Many of these mods utilize spell books or require active usage of one spell at a time. With MineBound we are attempting to allow users to create unique spell combinations through choice equipment instead of items which is the preferred method for most magic mods.

Please see https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/minebound for more information

one_liner: Early Interventions is a Python application that utilizes Machine Learning to predict student test scores for Salus University's Optometry program.
abstract: Early Interventions is a full-stack Python application that allows administrators of the Optometry program of Salus University to be able to view analytics based on historical student and course data. The application revolves around using Machine Learning and a logistic regression algorithm on student and course data to create predictions for pass-failure rate on exit exams as well as the weight of courses to the algorithm. The pass-fail predictions allow administrators to be able to identify students at risk of failing exit exams, and the weighting of courses helps to identify courses that have the greatest and least impact on a student's ability to pass the exit exams.

one_liner: Provides the ability to search any vulnerability located in our database to get a proper analysis that may not be obtainable through other databases available.
abstract:
There are numerous services that offer data modeling and summaries for cyber risk. CVE’s are readily available on Internet archives such as the NIST website. However, many of these products are lacking in two areas. First, they don’t provide analysis of how vulnerabilities may affect organizational operations or the specific goals of a piece of software or hardware. Secondly, there is no way for organizations to determine any chain of impacts that may occur. 

Our website and database seek to address these weaknesses by providing in-depth impact analysis for each vulnerability recorded in our database. Each vulnerability entry will provide impact analysis for certain categories of organizations (based on how different organizations use software or hardware related to the vulnerability). There will also be a summary of how the intended functions of a software are impacted by the vulnerability.

SoundFormX aims to solve the challenges musicians encounter in locating and acquiring top-quality audio files that match their particular requirements. At its core, SoundFormX simplifies the search process for musicians by providing them with an intuitive platform. Artists can effortlessly browse through a vast catalog of audio files, using various filters and search parameters to find the perfect sound for their creative projects. Whether they are looking for specific instruments, genres, BPM, or any other criteria, SoundFormX ensures that musicians can easily discover audio files that align with their unique requirements. SoundFormX goes beyond being just a marketplace for audio files. It also functions as a vibrant community platform that connects musicians and artists from all proficiency levels. Users can access a wealth of educational materials, including tutorials, guides, and articles, to enhance their knowledge and skills in music production. With SoundFormX, musicians and artists can save time and resources by accessing a one-stop shop for all their audio file needs, complete with educational resources and community support.​ SoundFormX also comes with an extensive administration panel, allowing the administrators to manage website content easily and without the need to alter code. When evaluating safety, one of the most significant factors people consider is the prevalence of crime in the area. Fortunately, Crime360° is a comprehensive application that collects crime data from various sources across cities in the United States of America. This interactive web dashboard allows users to access statistics on different types of crimes for cities across the country. Additionally, Crime360° provides helpful graphical visualizations that help users understand and contextualize crime data. By using Crime360°, members of the general public, government officials, law enforcement agencies, and other stakeholders can gain valuable insights into crime rates and trends in the USA. With this powerful tool, users can make informed decisions about where to live, invest, and visit while prioritizing safety and security.

one_liner: Calendar Expression (CALEX) is a novel annotation schema that could be useful for timeline reconstruction . This project will design and develop a system that uses a rule-based approach to identify and normalize temporal expressions in English text using CALEX annotation schema.
abstract:
Extracting and modeling temporal information from text is essential for
developing timelines and trajectories. However, identifying temporal and timerelated
expressions in the natural text has been a particularly challenging and
active area in computational linguistics.
Although many attempts at machine learning approaches have been
pursued, most state-of-the-art solutions still use rule-based systems to
normalize and provide a “value” for each temporal expression.
Calendar Expression (CALEX) is a novel annotation schema that could be
useful for timeline reconstruction. This project will design and develop a
system that uses a rule-based approach to identify and normalize temporal
expressions in English text using CALEX annotation schema.
The product is delivered as a Python third-party library that can be called to
output a calendar expression from the input text.

abstract:

We start with a web scraper that regularly scrapes data from popular job websites (currently only Indeed is supported) and stores the parsed data into a SQL database. The data then gets analyzed by our language processors to pull out useful information such as Keywords and Salary. Then we can display this information on a web dashboard, showing different statistics like most popular city for a certain job category, or most frequent keywords in a job category’s description.

one_liner: SpyPi is a command line utility for performing malware scanning on Python packages and facilitating the download and installation of packages via PyPi.

project_name: Automated Fish Shape Analysis for Machine Learning
one_liner: Building an image processing pipeline to perform machine learning analyses on digitized fish specimen repositories
abstract: Today's vast, online collections of digitized biological specimens have promising machine learning applications, but their metadata is often absent and sometimes erroneous. When present and accurate, morphological metadata in particular (specimen lengths, body part positions, etc.) provides valuable insight into species' geography, behaviors, and evolutionary histories. Researchers must compute this metadata for themselves, but it's prohibitively expensive to do it manually, so they need automated methods. This work focuses on automatically extracting metadata from one particular collection of fish specimens. We build an image processing pipeline for extracting fish outlines, a key morphological feature, and represent those outlines using elliptical Fourier descriptors. The resulting dataset is well suited for a variety of machine learning-based downstream analyses, one of the simplest being classification by genus and species.

project_name: A Vulnerability Assessment of Drexel’s Network
one_liner: The purpose of this vulnerability scan is to gather data across Drexel’s two public network address spaces.
abstract: As a team we scanned all areas of Drexel's network from the internal and external sides using various tools.  The 129.25.x.x/16 and 144.18.x.x/16 address spaces containing the entirety of Drexel's network cover over 131,000 potential hosts. This opens the doors for potential threat actors. Inside these address spaces, we found 363 of these hosts to be up, and scannable. Using NESSUS, NMAP, OpenVAS, and Shodan.io we were able to find a large variety of critical, high, medium, and low vulnerabilities within Drexel's various IP Addresses. We then took a deeper dive into each vulnerability to discover its threat level in the context of Drexel's environment. This was achieved by segregating each unique vulnerability and grouping it with the location it was found in Drexel's network. Based on our discoveries we devised a plan of action which appropriately tackled the network's most critical and essential vulnerabilities which we took the time to review and find remediations for.

one_liner: PortSploit is a one-stop shop reconnaissance tool allowing a user to input an organization and receive information about accessible IPs and open ports, pairing that with a known vulnerabilities database.
abstract:
Investigating different devices and vulnerabilities across the internet can result in cross-referencing multiple sites to get the information one needs. PortSploit aims to consolidate this information and combine the power of multiple tools to make reconnaissance and vulnerability hunting straightforward.  
PortSploit will utilize the power of Shodan to pull information on organizations such as accessible IPs, open ports, and other metadata and present it to the user. PortSploit will combine this data from the Shodan API with a local database containing port vulnerability information from SpeedGuide.net. The result is a view that provides a user with information about an organization’s open ports and potential vulnerabilities, all from one search. PortSploit also conveniently provides IP address information next to vulnerable ports, further simplifying the reconnaissance process. With the results, the user is able to sort the table and search for specific keywords. Additionally, if there is an IP Address that the user is interested in, they are able to click on that specific IP Address to only see that IP Address from the associated organization. Overall, PortSploit makes host discovery and vulnerability hunting a fast, easy, and more convenient process allowing for professionals to spend more time exploiting and less time hunting.

one_liner: Crystal Ball is a predictive analytics tool designed to help investors make informed investment decisions in specific industries. It uses various financial metrics and growth indicators to predict the performance of companies, and displays this information using interactive data
abstract:
Crystal Ball is a powerful predictive analytics tool developed to provide investors with valuable insights into the performance of companies within specific industries. It uses a combination of financial metrics and growth indicators such as earnings per share, revenue, and cash flow, along with other indicators such as overall sentiment, P/E ratio, market cap, and dividend rates, to predict the performance of companies in the future.

With Crystal Ball, investors can easily compare multiple stocks within a predefined industry and view historical and predicted stock prices. The tool also provides interactive data visualization tools that allow investors to track and visualize historical data trends, helping them to make informed investment decisions.

Crystal Ball also displays the inputs and outputs of the predictive model used, explaining their significance to investors. This feature helps investors to understand how the tool arrives at its predictions, enabling them to make informed decisions and adjust their investment strategies accordingly.

Overall, Crystal Ball is a comprehensive tool that leverages data visualization and predictive analytics to provide investors with valuable insights into the performance of companies within specific industries, helping them to make informed investment decisions.

one_liner: Propose a low-dimensional vectorial knowledge embedding representation for structured tabular datasets
abstract: This project proposes a method to transform structured data with missing values and categorical features into a low-dimensional vector representation that can be used in machine learning application. for the proposed low-dimensional embedding vector representation framework, we construct and evaluate the sequential neural network BiLSTM-Attention model and XGBoost model. We also evaluate the traditional logistic regression model and xgboost for the original non-multi-relational dataset with one-hot encodings. Our baseline model is the traditional logistic regression model for the original non-multi-relational dataset with one-hot encodings. Compared with logistic regression model, XGBoost and sequential neural network model BiLSTM-Attention can better explore the patterns of standard datasets. Furthermore, the evaluation results reflect the performance of XGBoost model using embeddings is better than the performance of xgboost  model using tabular dataset with one-hot encodings. This shows that the embeddings can convey more information.

one_liner: Learning Text Segmentation from Unlabeled Data
abstract: The digitalization of medical records has led to many attempts to devise ways to quickly and efficiently search through them via specialized algorithms. One way to improve this search efficiency is to segment documents into different sections and  classify each section so search terms can be first checked against relevant sections. Many models currently use a predefined list of sections and searches for words that match a list of indicators to classify a sentence as belonging to one section or the other, but this limits the model to only being used on documents with the same type of content. We propose a model that breaks documents into different sections without relying on specific word choice, and therefore can prove more versatile and applicable on other documents .

project_name: Enhancing Baseline Performance and Efficiency in ICD-9 Coding from Patient Discharge Notes
one_liner: This project aims to establish stronger baselines in text classification within the healthcare domain. We evaluated our proposed method in the task of assigning ICD codes from patient discharge notes.
abstract: The ICD coding process, which hospitals all over the world use to bill their patients’ visits, is very manual and tedious. Lots of research has gone into automating this process. In this project, we explore the effectiveness of less complex baselines for resolving the task of identifying ICD-9 codes using patient discharge notes. Despite the widespread use of deep learning models, we demonstrate that simpler methods can achieve comparable results while requiring less computational resources. Our results highlight the importance of thoroughly evaluating the performance of various models and methods for different tasks to avoid over-reliance on a particular approach. By considering less complex alternatives, researchers can improve the efficiency and practicality of their solutions while still achieving competitive results.

project_name: Structural Brain Network Site Differences and Connectome Data Harmonization
one_liner: Research on Structural Connectome Data Site Differences and Harmonization
abstract:
In recent years, researchers have become increasingly interested in brain networks, referred to as the connectome. A number of recent studies have reported that differences in structural and functional connectome data derived from various MRI scanners lead to systematic biases when comparing metrics (Kurokawa et al., 2021). Considerable research attention has been directed toward finding methods to reduce cross-scanner differences in raw MRI data while preserving differences between individuals, a concept called data harmonization. However, limited research exists on efficient methods for harmonizing connectomic data (i.e., minimizing differences between structural and/or functional connectomes of the same individual that are derived from raw data originating from different scanners).

In this research, we investigate methods to harmonize structural connectome data. First, we will preprocess raw diffusion MRI data to obtain structural connectomes. Then, we will perform a statistical analysis of the data to explore the presence of site differences across datasets, demonstrating the need for connectomic data harmonization. Finally, we will explore a method to harmonize the connectome data by i) examining the idea of ordinal connectomics, in which the order of edge weights is utilized rather than the actual edge weights to structural represent connectivity in the brain ii) exploring whether ordinal connectomics reduces site effect in structural connectomes.

project_name: TorchFL - A Python Library for Bootstrapping Federated Learning Experiments
one_liner: A Python library and a command-line tool for bootstrapping and benchmarking the federated learning experiments while abstracting the systems and implementation overhead for the users.
abstract: With the increased legislation around data privacy, federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising technique that allows the clients (end-user) to collaboratively train deep learning (DL) models without transferring and storing the data in a centralized, third-party server. We introduce TorchFL, a performant library for (i) bootstrapping the FL experiments, (ii) executing them using various hardware accelerators, (iii) profiling the performance, and (iv) logging the overall and agent-specific results on the go. Being built on a bottom-up design using PyTorch and Lightning, TorchFL provides ready-to-use abstractions for models, datasets, and FL algorithms, while allowing the developers to customize them as and when required. This paper aims to dig deeper into the architecture and design of TorchFL, elaborate on how it allows researchers to bootstrap the federated learning experience, and provide experiments and code snippets for the same. With the ready-to-use implementation of state-of-the-art DL models, datasets, and federated learning support, TorchFL aims to allow researchers with little to no engineering background to set up FL experiments with minimal coding and infrastructure overhead. The library is open-sourced on GitHub and can be found at https://github.com/torchfl-org/torchfl, the documentation can be found at https://torchfl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/, and the library can be downloaded at https://pypi.org/project/torchfl/.

abstract: The Bear Institute Scoresheets system is a web application for medical professionals to access medical scoresheets that aid in the diagnosis of rare diseases, such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) or Marfan syndrome. These scoresheets exist in many different Internet databases and can be difficult for a medical practitioner to locate in a timely manner, which can delay treatment timelines for patients. To solve this problem, this system shall provide a centralized location for these scoresheets, and they will be delivered in an interactive manner, such that the practitioner can fill in the scoresheet with information they collect from the patient.

one_liner: Research Project focusing on converting natural language questions to executable SQL queries
abstract: The research aims to resolve the schema linking problem in which words in natural language questions fail to map correctly to their corresponding references in the physical database. We aim to resolve this issue by using the logical data model and the associated names and descriptions of the schema elements in the physical model for better mapping with the words in the question. Moreover, the research project seeks to resolve creating valid join structures to be used in the FROM clause by acquiring the required schema elements for generating SQL query through mapping the question words, and then finding the paths that connects all the required elements by searching through different relationships that connects one element to another to construct a valid join statement. The key focus of this research is integrating the logical data model into the system for enhancing the performance of the conversion process.

one_liner: Account.ABLE is a mobile application that facilitates sustainable goal creation alongside an online community and accountability system with resources that help its users achieve those goals.
abstract: During the pandemic, many became much more introspective and realized that there is a lot of time on their hands. Through this, many identified the need for organization and goal setting such as making a budget, starting a design project, dieting, exercising, and even charity. We see the need for a system or product that would allow for the maintenance of accountability, motivation, and consistency. With an idea like Account.ABLE, an individual could accomplish all these things with a system that not only provides the means but also promotes such concepts. We want our users to be the desired version of themselves. To help the user with such a task, we’ve decided to create a calendar/task system for the visual organization of all the tasks throughout the month. Personalization of your account like custom color schemes, creating your own goals, and adding your own reminders, will make the app feel more pertained to the user. We believe that rewarding consistency is what keeps tasks going and not forgotten, so the badge system will help with staying disciplined in pursuit of goals and completing each task. We plan on honing in on each concept much more in-depth to identify the best ways to promote them on our app and encourage accountability.

one_liner: Refyne is a web application that offers AI text processing and data insights for all online customer to business communications.
abstract: The velocity at which data is produced has significantly increased over the past few years. Business owners who previously relied on word-of-mouth feedback now see the majority of customer sentiment fielded through electronic channels. Public figures who previously fielded mostly telephone calls primarily now have seen their inboxes overflow with comments, questions, and inquiries. These individuals have a demonstrated need for processing this high volume of textual information in an intelligent way without necessitating human input. Refyne offers an AI that converts text to data to allow customers to gather further and faster insights from their messages and feedback, stimulating more efficient communication from their customers to grow their business needs. Individuals can submit messages via email, embedded contact form, or CSV import to be processed by the application and sorted intelligently by an AI model. Paying subscribers can access messages via a message list, visual map, and messages analytics dashboard.

Gone are the days of manual searches and sifting through countless profiles. With FIND U, you take control by selecting your desired profession and the specific field you're interested in. FIND U's intelligent algorithm works tirelessly behind the scenes, web scraping information from online, as well as analyzing all that data, filtering it, and providing you with a simple list where you can identify individuals, their possible related skills, and possibly numbers and emails related to them.

Whether you're a student seeking mentorship, an industry professional looking for collaboration, or an enthusiast aiming to expand your network, FIND U caters to your unique needs. abstract: For our senior project, we are doing a research-type project that aims to explore the possibility of using quarterly historical fundamental ratios from the past 20 years to train various machine learning models and find use that model and fundamental ratios data gathered for stock to predict their quarterly return. The ratios data are collected from CRSP and FactSet covers many of the universal and industry-specific ratios. The machine learning model includes random forest, convolutional neural network, and logistic and linear regression. The best-performing model will be chosen in order to test out the model at the end newly reported fundamental ratio will be used to test out the algorithm.

one_liner: Synthetic data through embedding space sampling
abstract: The challenge of creating synthetic data from a source dataset is hiding individuals while keeping the general trends intact. Our synthetic data generator produces synthetic data by training embeddings and then sampling the resulting embedding space. We show that GANs and Conditional Probability Generators are not the only tools that can produce realistic synthetic data. Furthermore, our approach is generalizable across domains and does not suffer from the same constraints that other state-of-the-art methods do.

abstract:

Gephi is a powerful network visualization tool we utilized to help represent interconnected organizations, ICS devices, weaknesses, and mitigation tactics. Gephi has many great network visualization capabilities to understand complex networks, such as centrality, node degrees, and more network properties that can aid in identifying critical ICS components.
By leveraging this ICS threat modeling graph, we can analyze potential threats, recognize critical points, and mitigate security risks. With data collected from The Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and The National Vulnerability Database (NVD), this ICS Threat Modeling graph can assist in performing risk assessments and addressing weaknesses found in ICS environments.

one_liner: We conducted an internal and external penetration testing of the Franklin Institute to identify vulnerabilities to protect sensitive information and the reputation of the organization.
abstract: Our team performed internal and external penetration tests of the Franklin Institute, the most visited museum in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania that reaches more than one million people each year. During our external test, we used common open source intelligence techniques to identify publicly facing Franklin Institute owned systems. We performed on-site internal testing of the Franklin Institute by connecting to their internal network. We then leveraged common reconnaissance techniques like running Bloodhound to map the network, identify points of privilege escalation within the Active Directory structure, and locate exposed network interfaces. Our test allowed us to connect to security cameras, remotely manage and disable printers, and escalate our permissions to become an enterprise-level administrator. We presented a detailed report based on our findings to key stakeholders in the organization, and gave their technology teams a roadmap to remediating these vulnerabilities.

project_name: seeFretboard: Unlocking Boundless Possibilities for Music Education, Research, and Creative Exploration
one_liner: The seeFretboard Python library allows users to visualize guitar fretboards. Providing foundational music theory displays with intervals, chords, arpeggios, and scales. It also has features such as dynamic video creation of the visualized fretboards with integration of audio.
abstract:
The seeFretboard library is a powerful tool for creating and visualizing guitar fretboards, and has a wide range of applications in music theory education and research. This library is open source, meaning that anyone can contribute and build upon the existing codebase which makes it a collaborative and community-driven project with flexibilities and endless potential for growth and improvement. Users can incorporate it into their own websites or applications, or use it as a standalone tool for their own learning and research. This opens up many possibilities for customization and adaptation to different contexts and needs. With seeFretboard, users can easily create fretboard visualizations and customize various elements such as colors and styles. Additionally, seeFretboard can generate MIDI audio or the user can use their audio(mp3, wav, etc) and be combined with the generated fretboard video to create a complete multimedia and dynamic learning experience.

One of the main benefits of seeFretboard is its ability to generate fretboard images and videos quickly and accurately. It also has features for prediction vs ground truth. This is especially useful for music information retrieval researchers ,who are working on guitar transcription and need to generate many fretboard visualizations for their work. With seeFretboard, they can create these visualizations with code, saving time and effort compared to manual creation.

Looking ahead to future developments, seeFretboard has many exciting possibilities for educational applications. For example, the library could include features such as deliberate practice, repetition and reflection tools, quizzes, textbook, and games, and more advanced techniques for learning and generating and manipulating fretboard visualizations as well as AI/ML assistant or teacher. seeFretboard has the potential to make music education more accessible and engaging for a wide range of learners, from beginners to advanced musicians. Overall, seeFretboard empowers learners, researchers, and musicians with intuitive fretboard visualization and multimedia integration.

project_name: Improvement in Course Infrastructure and Equity
one_liner: Our project is centered around improving existing Computing Technology Lab environments by utilizing Drexel resources.
abstract: In Computing Technology (CT) courses at Drexel’s College of Computing and Informatics (CCI), there is a lack of equity among the lab environments and a need to review these environments' impact on students' learning experience. Some CT lab environments are costly, asking students to pay an extra fee for a third-party environment, which they only have temporary access to. Additionally, some of these lab environments may ask students to use free third-party software that is not compatible with student computers. Finally, third party labs limit a professors' control over the content of their labs and inhibit their ability to address students' technical issues. Having these issues in mind, our project aims to look at the weaknesses of three CT course lab environments and propose a solution utilizing free resources from CCI to improve the student experience and provide equity for all students.

project_name: Software Tests Generation by Parsing Natural Language
one_liner: Concurrently parse natural language using Combinatory Categorial Grammar (CCG). Generate software tests using this parsed sentence.
abstract:
This research is focused on developing a parser that parses Natural Language (English) using Combinatory Categorial Grammar (CCG). The parsed English Language is used to generate executable software tests. The existing machine learning implementations for parsing natural language are non-modular and difficult to repair. The other implementations use some type of probabilities and work with Context-Free Grammar. We do not have enough statistics to be able to work with probabilities with the current CCG lexicon as it does not include enough software and testing-related terms.
Our parser is based on Cocke–Younger–Kasami (CYK) chart parsing algorithm. We have applied classic ideas from linguistics to parse natural language and generate test cases. While there are existing parsers that do the work, they aren’t very efficient. For this, we have made the parsing algorithm concurrent for more efficient results.

one_liner: Classification of sinusitis severity from WSI (Whole Slide Images) through advanced deep learning techniques
abstract:
The Digital Pathology Web App is a sophisticated online platform designed for the classification of sinusitis based on whole slide image inputs. With a user-friendly interface and advanced features, the web application offers a comprehensive solution for pathologists, researchers, and developers involved in digital pathology analysis.

Built using ElectronJS and React, the web application provides a responsive and intuitive frontend interface. Users can easily upload their whole slide images and apply various pre-processing techniques for enhanced analysis. The drag-and-drop functionality simplifies the image upload process, while flexible processing technique selection and adjustable parameters ensure optimal customization.

The backend infrastructure leverages state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to accurately analyze and classify sinusitis based on the provided whole slide images. Real-time verification capabilities allow pathologists and technicians to review and validate the system's findings, ensuring confidence in the analysis results.

To streamline the development and training of machine learning models, the platform incorporates a Model Development Environment (MDE). With pre-installed requirements and dependencies, the MDE eliminates compatibility issues across different operating systems and processor architectures, enabling efficient model building and deployment.

Advanced image processing techniques, such as Felzenszwalb, Quickshift, and SLIC segmentation algorithms, are integrated into the system. These techniques identify regions of interest (ROIs) within the whole slide images, improving the precision and performance of the classification models. By focusing on relevant ROIs, the analysis results are optimized for accurate and reliable diagnoses.

Data acquisition and processing are seamlessly handled by the platform's Unified Image Reader (UIR). The UIR provides a unified interface for reading large-scale images by regions, facilitating efficient processing of massive image datasets that exceed memory limitations.

The Custom Dataset (CD), an extension of PyTorch's Dataset, lies at the core of the system. CD incorporates advanced filtration algorithms and implements the Dark Region Mapping technique to handle dynamically sized datasets. This ensures that only relevant regions pass through the filtration process, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of subsequent analysis stages.

With its focus on speed, flexibility, and verifiability, the Digital Pathology Web App revolutionizes digital pathology analysis. It empowers pathologists, researchers, and developers with advanced tools and technologies to improve diagnostic precision and enhance patient care.

Discover the power of the Digital Pathology Web App and experience the convergence of artificial intelligence and image processing in the field of digital pathology analysis. Join us on this transformative journey as we push the boundaries of accuracy and efficiency in pathology diagnostics.

one_liner: Player 2 - the Gamer’s Companion: a social networking and team-building app for gamers.
abstract:
For the over 2 billion online video gamers worldwide, supporting a passion for games can be a convoluted endeavor. While gamers use platforms like Twitch, YouTube, Discord, Reddit, and various social media to empower their gaming, numerous gaps in gaming support still exist – such as a lack of advanced teammate matchmaking, a root cause of gaming’s notorious toxicity issue.

Player 2 offers a comprehensive solution for a gamer’s social networking and team-building needs. Player 2 leads with Compatibility Matchmaking, a proprietary process by which users can find teammates with compatible playstyles and personalities. Player 2’s Playgrounds offer an expanded Reddit/Discord hybrid section that provides unparalleled support for gaming communities, developers, streamers, and media. Additional functions of Player 2 include LFG - for users to find teammates for immediate activities, Messaging - easy/secure communication with Player 2 friends, and Game Hub - the scrolling focal point of one’s favorite gaming content.

one_liner: My Care Team is a web app that allows patients to learn more about their Care Providers and make more meaningful connections for the benefit of patients, their families, and hospital staff.
abstract:
Our stakeholders at Children's National need a better way to introduce clinicians and their roles to young patients and their families. When they arrive at the hospital, families often have no concept of who's who between the trainees, rotating attendings, shift nurses, consultants, and specialists and often do not understand what those roles mean. When a provider enters the room, it's challenging and awkward for patients and their families to try and read staff badges and get to know their clinicians, all while processing the other medical information they're being confronted with. Children's National is looking for a way for patients to study providers even after they've left the room, giving them more time to process who they are and learn to recognize them and understand their roles.

To address these problems, our team has developed My Care Team: an application that serves to introduce patients to their clinicians. Patients will be able to browse all care providers at Children's National, and have the option to filter by name, department, and spoken languages. Each Care Provider has their own profile that contains information such as the Care Provider's name, image, title, department, and pronouns, as well as their biography. Patients can then add clinicians to their Care Team, which effectively allows them to keep a log of all the clinicians they interact with during their stay. Using our application will allow patients to learn more about their care providers, provide a way for users from a non-clinical perspective to familiarize themselves with the hospital, and give young patients and their families more control over a situation that can often feel unfamiliar and intimidating. 

Another important aspect of the My Care Team application is the Console, which is utilized by both system administrators and content administrators. The first tool in the Console is User Role Management, which allows for system administrators to perform operations on accounts for other system administrators as well as content administrators. Additionally, there is the Configurations aspect, which is utilized by content administrators to manipulate properties used for care provider information such as department, role, title, etc. Finally, the last tool in the Console is working with Care Providers, which allows for content administrators to create, update, and delete the Care Provider accounts that patients access.

one_liner: A bus shuttle tracking platform for their students to better utilize the Drexel bus system
abstract:
Currently, Drexel students face many issues when it comes to accessing and
using the shuttle system on a day-to-day basis. As a team we have been able to identify three major issues the student body is facing regarding the current Drexel shuttle system:

- Students have no way of knowing exactly if/when the next shuttle is to arrive at a given bus stop, especially during rush hour traffic 
- Students may not be aware of the various routes/stops both in the University City and Center City areas.
- Due to construction stops being changed to temporary locations, students are often unaware of these changes.


The project aims to provide an interactive bus tracking map system that will display accurate currently operating bus locations and ETA at each stops along their route. We want to develop a solution to the problems at hand faced by students taking the Drexel shuttles daily, mainly being exact bus arrival time, available bus stops, and any updates to route changes.

one_liner: Explores the overpayment of the VCG auction mechanism in a complex algorithmic setting
abstract:
The Uncapacitated Facility Location Problem focuses on minimizing facility opening costs and client connect costs over a set of given facilities. We examine the private information setting of this problem where facility opening costs are only known to the facilities themselves and we must determine their value through an auction.

We use the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves auction to find the optimal solution, and our main focus is establishing a bound on the frugality ratio of this problem, where frugality is defined as total overpayment compared to the second-cheapest disjoint solution. Our research resolves this problem by proving an upper bound of 2 on the frugality ratio via a charging argument, and establishes that this bound is tight by providing an instance of Uncapacitated Facility Location that achieves a frugality ratio of 2.

project_name: DECEPTICONS ATTACK! ATTACKING AND DEFENDING CYBER DEFENSE SYSTEMS USING TRANSFORMERS
one_liner: Using transformers to generate and detect cyber threat intelligence
abstract:
Open source text has become an integral part of most cyber defense systems, most of these systems rely on this data for the latest open-source intelligence (OSINT). These systems use natural language processing techniques to extract information from the text, called cyber threat intelligence (CTI), to create knowledge graphs that are used in downstream defense tasks. Since the training text data is open source, it is vulnerable to manipulation by adversaries. Adversaries can potentially bombard the usual forums for data collection like blog posts, chat forums, etc with false CTI and change the training data so that the models learn incorrect patterns and serve the adversary's needs. 

This project investigates the use of transformer models to generate false CTI and using the same models to classify any given CTI as human-written or fake. We evaluate different classification methods and explore the efficacy of representation learning using large-scale language models.

one_liner: Implement a fully homomorphic encryption scheme capable of running any function in an encrypted setting.
abstract:
Encryption schemes are widely used for purposes such as data privacy, data integrity, security, and verifying identity. Recent advances in cryptography have allowed for fully homomorphic encryption schemes, which unlike prior schemes can support computation of any function on encrypted data. These schemes have a real-world use case, namely in cloud computing: homomorphic encryption schemes allow for third-party servers to perform intensive computations without needing to expose the underlying data. Such schemes would be invaluable to businesses (such as those in healthcare and government) that would like to leverage cloud computing processing power while protecting data privacy.

In this project we implement in Python an integer-based fully homomorphic encryption scheme where functions are run as virtual binary circuits. We illustrate through our implementation the details of homomorphic encryption and how these schemes work. Furthermore, we provide support for the concept of "bootstrapping", where, by emulating the decryption algorithm inside an encrypted circuit, we are able to maintain error bounds and fully support any function. Finally, we programmatically verify correctness of our implementation and demonstrate how we may leverage bootstrapping in performing large computations.

one_liner: Metropolis IoT is an Internet of Things (IoT) solution that aims to provide aggregated real time environmental data to cities and companies.
abstract:
As populations continue to rise, there is increasing strain on services provided by cities and companies. As such, a company’s or city’s response time plays an important role in the constant maintenance and upkeep of said services. Therefore, the integration of IoT solutions that allow service providers to constantly monitor their service(s) become increasingly important.

Metropolis IoT aims to provide a IoT solution for gathering and aggregating environmental data. Allowing cities or companies to better monitor surrounding environmental data and use that to their benefit. For instance, cities could implement water sensors to look detect changes in water pressure and water level to better triangulate possible leaks or use the same sensors to determine pollutants in the water system. Metropolis IoT aims to allow users to compare and view their environmental data on a online dashboard.

one_liner: Make use of machine learning to help pathologists identify the density of the eosinophil cells in digital slides of human nasal tissue.
abstract:
The Digital Pathology project aims to use computer neural networks in an effort to reduce the time-consuming activity of analyzing digital slides during diagnosis of Sinusitis. This project was initially started in 2018 as a Senior Design project and then improved upon in 2019 by another Senior Design team. Partnering with the pathology department at the University of Pennsylvania, they collected data, built interfaces to help pathologists categorize the data, and made great steps towards achieving their goal of creating a tool to output the density of the eosinophil cells in digital slides of human nasal tissue. 
    The  new 2021/2022 Digital Pathology team is working to continue the project the previous two teams laid out. By analyzing, reworking, and expanding upon the original code base, the current Digital Pathology team looks to improve the original project both in accuracy of cell detection and in identification time to where practicing pathologists may benefit from the use of the tool in actual medical cases.

one_liner: A personalized assistant that helps individuals gain greater independence through digital prompting.
abstract:
A substantial amount of individuals experience difficulties completing daily tasks, such as washing hands, brushing teeth, and closing the door. These people are often in need of a gentle reminder to help them complete these activities. Being able to accomplish these tasks without a guardian allows for them to gain a newfound sense of independence and responsibility.

CareGiver is an iOS application designed to assist individuals who need additional daily support. By sending reminder notifications, the application helps users become more accustomed to independence. In addition, this also alleviates the need for constant monitoring by the caregiver. Ultimately, CareGiver is the ideal solution to lend a helping hand to both parties.

one_liner: Vulnerability scans and penetration tests can help security analysts best identify the major gaps in their network so that they can mitigate them and make their environment more secure
abstract:
Many organizations have vulnerability management teams to best assess the integrity of their security controls and security gaps which helps identify the risks present. The best way to understand the different gaps within your environment is by performing scans/penetration tests on both the internal and external environments. By going at Drexel’s environment with two different perspectives, a student at the university who wants to increase their privilege, and as an external attacker that wants to gain access to Drexel’s resources, we can best understand the vulnerabilities present in Drexel’s environment. 
    After collecting all the data from the scans and tests we will be able to create metrics and displays that show all the vulnerabilities found and highlight the 5-10 most severe. Along with pulling resources from MITRE ATT&CK will we be able to create a report on best practices and mitigation techniques to reduce the risks found from our vulnerability assessment, ultimately making Drexel’s environment more secure.

one_liner: Firewall Rule Data Enrichment and Visualization Tool.
abstract:
In the world of Network Security, a Firewall acts as a checkpoint for traffic moving between networks, and this is formulated as a set of rules.  When an analyst needs to look into these rule sets, they are likely leveraging tools which output excel spreadsheets.  We sought to produce a tool which is able to enrich these reports, so that security analysts can better understand the access across a network environment. Report2Map aims to highlight problems such as access overlap and access creep, which can prove detrimental to a network by enabling unauthorized access between hosts.  Our tool looks to simplify the analysis process of firewall rule sets, by reducing the reliance on spreadsheets- and instead enriching this same data with a visualized ontology. 

The backbone of any product which focuses on the enrichment of data is the input data itself. In the case of our tool, we focus on Firewall Rule Reports, a quite common piece of information across teams focused on network security. Firewall rule reports contain a list of firewall rules, which detail the network traffic which is permitted across a network’s firewalls. These rules sit on firewalls, which sit between layers of a network. The most common structure of a rule is simple; a Source IP address, a Destination IP address, a port, and whether the traffic is allowed, or disallowed. You can imagine, with how many devices typically exist on a network, how complicated your list of rules can get. 

Network analysts spend tons of time working with compilations of these rules, In example, the firewall rule reports that was mentioned previously. These typically take the form of Excel Spreadsheets, lines and lines of rules. Getting into the rules and extracting actionable information is hard to do manually, and there are many tools which aide in this process, but none fill our specific niche. We aim to take this data and provide the user with an ontology of their rules. To further empower the user, we provide filters which the user can leverage to tailor visibility on specific IP Addresses, as well as ports. The intent is that through use of these user-centric features, the resulting output is an enrichment of the provided input- allowing for an analyst to better understand the firewall rules in each environment.

one_liner: A vulnerability alert system that can be used by security experts to stay current on emerging threats and vulnerabilities to improve information security and mitigation efforts. Visit https://vans.titanite.me/vans/register.php to create an account with VANS today!
abstract:
One of the many challenges being faced in technology today are the numerous threats and vulnerabilities being encountered with on-premise, enterprise, and cloud systems. Specifically, those targeting web sites, applications, databases, networks, infrastructure, appliances and the gamut of IoT devices. Since 60% of data breaches take several weeks to be identified (O'Driscoll, 2022), security experts face immense pressure to prevent data breaches and develop proactive mitigation strategies in a timely manner. When an organization falls victim to a cybersecurity attack, they will have to deal with the immediate monetary impact in addition to the reputational impact that will reduce consumer confidence in their product and the ability to protect sensitive information. 

VANS provides security experts with the ability to monitor and stay current with the latest threat and vulnerability data from a variety of sources fused into one aggregate feed. Users can utilize the VANS Web Portal to search or filter for threats and vulnerabilities by keywords, products or vendors. Furthermore, by leveraging the embedded automation awareness tools, VANS allows users to subscribe to receiving timely notifications on targeted threats and vulnerabilities via email or push notification on the Android app. Through data visualization tools, VANS will further expand its capabilities providing real-time threat and vulnerability statistics to its user base. In an effort to preemptively mitigate and establish a proactive security posture, it has become necessary to collate and consolidate data security intelligence from a number of reputable disclosed security sources into one database. The identification of relevant threats and vulnerabilities can improve efforts to prioritize mitigation and patch strategies.

one_liner: Flourish is an app that provides care recommendations about your plant, paired with a sensor that monitors it's vitals
abstract:
Flourish is an app that provides care recommendations about your plant, paired with a sensor that detects soil moisture, sunlight, temperature, and humidity.

The application can be run on any iOS or Android device, offering an intuitive way to view information regarding your plants, such as its current health, species-specific attributes, historical data, and more. Push notifications are used to remind you to keep the plant's conditions optimal for their growth. Users can also use the explore page to find useful advice about various plants to further their knowledge.

Paired with the application is an IoT device that has four sensors to help keep track of your plant's vitals. These sensors measure temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and sunlight. The device transmits data to the server over WiFi, and is commissioned over Bluetooth.

one_liner: Our app is designed to track putts made by golfers on various putting greens and make suggestions to optimize future putts using statistics.
abstract:
According to 18Birdies.com the average golfer takes at least 40 putts per round. The easiest way to reduce your score is to reduce the average number of putts taken at each hole.  We aim to do just that by creating an app that's able to see the optimal putt to a particular hole. Utilizing iPhone 12’s cameras and LIDAR sensor, the app would project an augmented reality overlay similar to those seen in TV coverage of professional golf. 

Using computer vision, the app would track each putt to provide analytics and other important criteria to help golfers improve and measure their putting consistency over time. The app is designed to help golfers make their putts and assist them in making future putts by giving suggestions. Additionally, golf coaches can measure their teams putting ability over the season.  The app tracks statistics made by each golfer, with putting sessions where golfers can see each individual sessions, loaded with statistics of their putts.

one_liner: A real-time, feasible solution to matching celebrity images from your screen, using just your phone!
abstract:
Often times, you may consume some element of media on your screen whether it is a movie or show, and not know who the celebrity is within that. Place That Face is a mobile application built for both iOS and Android platforms, which aims to tackle this problem in an intelligent manner, using a machine learning facial recognition algorithm and data analysis to quickly identify the celebrity via image captured or uploaded. Users can generate their own profile based on their genre preferences, which can help further narrow down the celebrity they may want to identify. The application offers many notable features such as being able to bookmark search results, and see where these celebrities may have worked, in other movies or shows. Aside from celebrity identification, the aim of this application is to cater these results to the individual using this application, hence the intelligence or AI being used. 

The goal of this application is not only to cater to avid media consumers that are keen to identify celebrities, but also to simply demonstrate that this could be the Google for celebrity images, and though similar technologies and infrastructure have been built and deployed, it is worth exploring how applications of such resources can be leveraged to build a product that targets a specific niche, and builds a community of committed users. The feedback of the users is also highly considered for improving the accuracy for matches made in the future, and for an overall better user experience.

one_liner: A PC-based, frontier themed, multi-player kart battle game featuring tether mobility and vehicle-altering power ups.
abstract:
The video game market today has no shortage of online multiplayer games: from strategy games to shooters and everything in between, there is a game with a thriving user base to suit any genre's needs. The problem with many of the existing titles is that they don’t always strike a great balance with the number of mechanics they provide to the player. For example, Rocket League is still one of the most popular party games, with the premise simply being soccer with cars. There are no other mechanics in the game beside driving and boosting a car to move a ball into a goal. Contrast this with another massively popular game such as Fortnite, where not only is skill required during gun play, but there’s also the need to build structures to navigate and protect oneself, strategize for looting and upgrading one’s loadout, dealing with an ever shrinking stage, all this while only having one life for the duration of the match.

With Fool's Gold Frenzy, we developed a game that has a balance of fun mechanics that engage the player, without overwhelming them. The gameplay is reminiscent of classic games such as Mario Kart, in that it’s inviting for new players to pick up, while also creating a higher skill ceiling that rewards players who spend time understanding the game's more advanced maneuvering. 

At its core, Fool's Gold Frenzy is an arena based kart battler where 4-6 players compete to collect the most gold in the midst of a gold rush. Players have access to combinable power-ups that are found on the stage or stolen from other players. Player can also get creative with the game's lasso tether mechanic for momentum based maneuvering around the stage.

one_liner: Nature’s Grave is a top down 2D action game where the player controls a spirt of nature who must revive a dead world on the brink.
abstract:
Nature's Grave is a 2D top-down action game focused on intense combat interactions and evocative environments. You navigate the world as a nature spirit with the goal of defeating the blighted monsters that have poisoned the world. Fight your way through the corruption and bring life back to a dead land!
There is a recent surge in the popularity of 2D top down action games. From Hyper Light Drifter to 2020 Game of the year nominee Hades, this style remains as relevant as it was in days of the original Legend of Zelda. We intend to create a game inpsired by this classic style with an injection of our unique aesthetic.

one_liner: 3 v 3 Online multiplayer competitive tag and platformer with abilities
abstract: Rushdown is an online multiplayer 3 vs 3, 3rd-person freeze-tag game. The rules are simple - catch the other players or avoid being caught in the allotted time given. Players can use anything at their disposal, whether that be movement, abilities, or other options available on the map. Teams will play a best of 5-round series, switching between catcher and evader at halftime. In the event of a tie, the players will enter sudden death in which they have the opportunity to play each side one more time. If both teams end up in a tie within sudden death, the game ends in a tie. For more information, please check out "rushdownsite.wordpress.com"

one_liner: A multiplayer party brawler game featuring a mishmash of combat gadgets and robot dismemberment!
abstract:
Welcome to Lockjaw, where it's every robot for themselves in the tournament of the century!

Grab parts laying around and knock them off others! Starting off with just your robotic core, scavenge parts to ensure your robot’s survival. With four slots on every robot, mix and match parts—each engagement is sure to grind some gears. Pack some heat with the dodgeball launcher to send robots flying, or deliver a powered-up punch with The Tenderizer! 

Every gadget can make an impact in the dynamic battles of Lockjaw. Gear up and join the robotic rumble today!

abstract: The Universal Trading Card Database project aims to establish a centralized database for all types of trading cards. This is done by scraping data and images from many online sources. The project takes all of the data from the different websites and normalizes them to fit into a universal schema where they can all be housed under one database. The universal database contains a wide range of trading cards from both sports and non-sports categories.
